lessons.title: expect/actual: Sharing Logic, Not UI
lessons.content: KMP lets you share business logic (networking, data models, repositories, validation) across Android and iOS while keeping native UI on each platform. `expect` declares an API in shared code without an implementation; each platform provides an `actual` implementation. Real scenario: sharing a DateFormatter across Android and iOS, since each platform has different native date APIs (java.time vs Foundation's DateFormatter) but the shared code just needs a consistent interface.

lessons.title: What Belongs in Shared vs Platform Code
lessons.content: A practical rule most production KMP codebases follow: put networking clients (Ktor client works on both platforms), data models, business/validation logic, and repository implementations in commonMain. Keep UI (Compose Multiplatform is an option, but many teams keep native SwiftUI/Jetpack Compose), platform-specific storage APIs, and anything touching platform SDKs (camera, biometrics, notifications) in platform-specific source sets. This is exactly the LessonRepository/domain-layer split you already have in your Android app - it's the same abstraction KMP asks you to make, just extended across platforms.
